deterministic_findings.title: eval/exec call in added code

reviewer_reports.summary: The evidence sidecar writer introduces a reachable crash path when a report contains non-dict entries in finding lists, while the verifier explicitly tolerates such malformed entries. This regression can break report writing for inputs that previously survived verification and iteration.

findings.title: write_report now crashes on non-dict finding entries that verifier and iterator paths tolerate
findings.evidence: The new writer loops over every item in each finding list and unconditionally calls walk_finding, but walk_finding then executes membership tests against the raw object. For a non-dict entry, the added line 'if 'dispute' in f or 'adjudication' in f:' raises TypeError on supported Python when f is not iterable, making write_report fail instead of skipping malformed entries as _iter_evidence_refs do
findings.evidence_quote: if "dispute" in f or "adjudication" in f:
findings.recommendation: Guard this branch with an isinstance(f, dict) check before any membership tests, or return early for non-dict values after the existing seen logic. Keep writer behavior aligned with _iter_evidence_refs, which already skips non-dict findings safely.

reviewer_reports.summary: I found one correctness regression in the new precedent matching logic that can incorrectly suppress live findings after unrelated same-name functions change elsewhere in the file.

findings.title: Function-level precedent can match the wrong callee when multiple functions share a name
findings.evidence: The function-key builder indexes callees only by bare name, so later definitions overwrite earlier ones and call sites are matched to whichever same-named function was seen last. In a supported Python module with two different methods or nested functions sharing a name, a precedent for one enclosing function can be treated as still valid or invalid based on an unrelated same-named function elsewhe
findings.recommendation: Key callees by qualified name or by lexical scope instead of bare `n.name`, and resolve `ast.Attribute` calls against the enclosing class/function scope so same-named functions in other scopes cannot alias each other in the precedent hash.

reviewer_reports.summary: The v0.10.0 integration diff introduces supported-platform manifest, severity rubric, dispute ladder with Tech Lead adjudication, amendment fixes for timeout and probe-loop bounds, archived-record exclusion, and evidence sidecars — all 361 tests pass with no new reliability defects.
I did not find a correctness or security issue that is demonstrably introduced by this diff chunk alone.

The diff adds evidence sidecar infrastructure, adjudication timeout guards, probe round bounds, and archived-record exclusion — all changes are consistent with the test suite and supported-platform policy. No unreachable defects or reliability risks were found.

The change introduces several reliability and correctness risks: unbounded retry loops without dedup/cooldown, missing timeouts on Tech Lead calls, evidence_quote truncation that destroys full-text integrity, and archived-text classification logic that may misclassify findings. These issues can cause alert floods, pipeline hangs, and data loss in production.
